newsitem.title: USA: Reliance Steel says estimate cut hurt stock.
newsitem.headline: Reliance Steel says estimate cut hurt stock.

text.p: Reliance Steel & Aluminum Co said Wednesday its share price was hurt by the decision by Prudential Securities analyst Ken Hoffman to cut his fourth quarter and 1997 earnings estimates for the company.
It said its share price fell about 11 percent Tuesday. In early trading Wednesday the stock was up 1/2 to 30-1/8.
Reliance Steel President David Hannah said he expects to report record sales and earnings for 1996.
"We believe that 1996 will be a record year for Reliance in terms of sales and earnings," Hannah said in a statement.

He said the Prudential revised estimates take into account the potential negative impact of last-in-first-out (LIFO) accounting in 1997 due to anticipated increased metal prices. Hannah said such increased prices would not result in any LIFO benefit in 1997.
"We expect 1996 net income to include approximately $3.5 million, or $0.34 per share, from LIFO as a result, primarily, of falling aluminum and stainless steel prices," he said.
"Based on current business conditions, we are also optimistic that 1997 operating results, before the effect of LIFO accounting, will be better than in 1996."
